content.comment_body: Hello. I am using a [product_name] with article number [article_no] and [product_name] software version [version_no]. Is it possible to create a program that, during a process, records the time when an input (for example, I1) is switched on and off, counts how many times it was activated, and tracks the duration of each activation? At the end of the process, I need access to all these records.
To achieve this, you may need a [product_name] with datalogging capability. The hardware you are currently using may not support this function directly.

You can store this information in text fields. Use a counter for each new record and assign each record to its own numbered text field. On this series, you can have a maximum of 10 text fields for your device. Please refer to the attached example for preliminary data saving.

Hello [user_name], You can continue using your current [product_name] with article number [article_no] and [product_name] software version [version_no]. Review the function group 'counter' and apply the 'hours counter' block. The help documentation provides parameter descriptions. On the right side of the interface, you can see the elapsed time that input I1 was high, and below, when I1 was low. You can view an example in the attachment. If you want to display the values on the device screen, follow [user_name]'s suggestion. If you wish to view the data on a PC, you will need to export it. Instructions for this can be found in the forum. Did this solve your problem? Regards

Hello. Thank you for the responses. Since I need to view the data directly on the device, I will try the suggestion from [user_name]. Ten records should be sufficient. Does the device keep all ten text fields in memory, or are they overwritten each time a new one is generated?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are working to monitor and record input signal changes (on/off events, counts, and durations) with a specific [product_name] hardware and software. Data storage and visualization limitations on the device lead to discussions about possible hardware upgrades and alternatives using the current setup.
analysis.user_expectations: The main expectation is to log and retrieve time-stamped data for input events (activation, deactivation, count, elapsed time) using the available [product_name] hardware and software, while maintaining an accessible history either on the device or through exported files.
